Overbroad Definition of Non-Protected Speech (Regulation 4392, Section II.B) • The Policy Language: CCSD Regulation 4392 states: "when District employees engage in speech that arises directly from their work, the speech is not protected... speech is considered to arise from an employee's work when the speech concerns a subject matter that primarily involves the employee's job or duties." It further claims that "specific issues, concerns, or grievances regarding a District employee's work are not considered matters of public concern." • The Violation: This definition overreaches Garcetti v. Ceballos. Garcetti applies strictly to speech made pursuant to official job duties (e.g., writing an official internal memo), NOT speech about a workplace topic made in an employee's private capacity. Declaring that anything "involving" a job cannot be a matter of public concern unconstitutionall...

sourceReferences.label: Primary source
sourceReferences.snippet: I respectfully ask the Board to delay approval of the North Lyon County Power District Ordinance and reconsider moving forward with the Greenlink Project until all potential impacts have been thoroughly evaluated. The ordinance lays the foundation for significant expansion of electrical infrastructure to support large industrial users, including data centers, but many questions remain unanswered. Before approving projects of this scale, the public deserves a full understanding of the potential environmental impacts, effects on wildlife and open space, future industrial expansion, demands on our infrastructure, and any potential long-term health considerations associated with large-scale electrical development. sourceReferences.snippet: 2.5 BASE CONDITIONS MODELING SUMMARY The base (or existing) conditions FLO-2D models were created using the best available information for land cover, land use, topography, and hydrology that were available at the time of the study. Every effort was made to ensure the models represented existing conditions as of the date of the LiDAR topography. Photographs and anecdotal flood information collected from the residents within the community were used to help calibrate and verify the modeling results. Like all models, these base conditions FLO-2D models are a simulation of potential conditions that could occur during a range of storm events. The models cannot exactly replicate actual, observed storm events at all locations within the watershed due to the vast number of variables that change with each unique storm event. sourceReferences.snippet: 5.1 SUMMARY Through the development of the base (or existing) conditions hydrology and hydraulics and the classification of existing flood hazards, flood prone areas were identified. To protect these areas, a total of three mitigation alternatives were proposed, designed (to a 15% level), and evaluated for their benefit. These alternatives consisted of local structures (i.e., their benefits fall with a small area close to the improvement and their design is on a much smaller level). The estimated benefits were weighed with each structure’s project cost, and a preliminary prioritization plan is proposed.

Chairman Karr inquired whether the copper service replacement projects mentioned by Director Poindexter were funded through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA). He stated that previous ARPA funding has been fully expended, specifically on earlier meter replacement initiatives.

sourceReferences.snippet: VI. BRIEFING: A. Briefing to/from the Commission and the Executive Director. (for discussion only) Director Hughes – Mynt Phase II is rolling out on Monday, December 8, 2025. We are currently four days away from rollout. sourceReferences.snippet: I. Isolated artifacts: An isolated artifact is defined herein as a single artifact or pieces from a single artifact, i.e., 10 pieces of glass from a single bottle. An isolated artifact is considered single and unassociated when separated by 30 meters or more from any other artifact. For example, two flakes of the same or different raw material separated by 29 meters would be documented as a site. Ten pieces of glass from a single bottle spread across 31 meters would be an isolate. Isolates are not recorded on a site form, but are listed in a table designated by number, description, and location.

Elizabeth Seibold has requested to transfer full ownership of Tri-Motor, LLC to her son, Scott Seibold, and both parties have confirmed the request via email. sourceReferences.snippet: 3. Spot Zoning Inconsistencies in the Downtown Mixed Use Expansion If Downtown Mixed Use (DTMU) zoning is planned to extend north to Winnie Lane, there must be consistent application. As currently proposed, John and Corbett Streets are included in the DTMU designation, yet Rice Street—directly between them—is completely excluded without any stated reason. I have raised this issue multiple times at Master Plan review meetings and through the online portal and have yet to receive any explanation. This kind of arbitrary spot zoning raises serious concerns about transparency and fairness in how zoning boundaries are being drawn. Residents deserve consistent and accountable planning—not piecemeal decisions that affect property values and neighborhood character without public justification.

sourceReferences.snippet: 9. Information Only – First Quarter Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Athletics Financial Report, UNLV, UNR, CSN, and TMCC – (Continued) Regent Goodman asked how the Athletic Department got to a $27 million deficit. UNLV Vice President Wyman stated there was a policy change associated with the reporting of deficit on accounts. They previously did not have to report on certain capital projects associated with gift revenue at the account level. The second part was faulty assumptions. The previous Chief Financial Officer worked with the Athletic Department to develop a model for the annual budget which had some anticipations for unrestricted gift-giving, but the Department received the funds via restricted gift-giving. Because UNLV had to pivot from unrestricted to restricted, that drove the deficit.

FOR DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE ACTION: REVIEW AND APPROVE AMENDMENTS TO AIRPORT RULES AND REGULATIONS, CCMC TITLE 19, AS TO THROUGH-THE-FENCE PROVISIONS AND GENERAL ACCESS PROVISIONS. (S. TACKES) Staff Summary: Airport staff has proposed amendments to Title 19, Section 19.03 to update the Airport Through-the-Fence (TTF) rules to address adjacent off-airport -- 1 of 3 -- hangar projects with TFF access, related definitions, operations, fees and enforcement provisions. The changes allow for Adjacent Hangar Associations and the terms for TTF access, and fees. In addition, the amendments propose a change to Section 19.02 to specify that gate controls apply to persons, vehicles and aircraft, with fees to cover the costs of operation. After adoption by the Authority for use on the Airport, these changes shall be presented to the Board of Supervisors for inclusion in the City Municipal Code.

sourceReferences.snippet: 4. PUBLIC COMMENTS (5:01:05) – Chairperson Preston entertained public comments. sourceReferences.label: Primary source
sourceReferences.snippet: I. Isolated artifacts: An isolated artifact is defined herein as a single artifact or pieces from a single artifact, i.e., 10 pieces of glass from a single bottle. An isolated artifact is considered single and unassociated when separated by 30 meters or more from any other artifact. For example, two flakes of the same or different raw material separated by 29 meters would be documented as a site. Ten pieces of glass from a single bottle spread across 31 meters would be an isolate. Isolates are not recorded on a site form, but are listed in a table designated by number, description, and location.

A single feature unassociated with other features or artifact scatters that are undateable (e.g., a prospect pit, a claim marker, an adit, a shaft). An isolated or unassociated feature is considered single and unassociated when separated by 30 meters or more from any other feature or artifact. Isolated or unassociated features need not be recorded on a site form, but are listed in a table designated by number, description, and location. B. If features are elements to a historic district, they are not isolated or unassociated. If an isolated feature is unique because of its construction (elaborate stonework claim marker) or distinctive qualities, the feature must be recorded as a site and evaluated for eligibility. Isolated features that have potential data (fire hearth) must be recorded as a site and evaluated for eligibility.
